semantics.p: High-level transparent latch: follows a while clock=1, holds while clock=0. Evidence: p tracks a at 90..110 ns and holds 1 throughout 115..140 ns.
semantics.q: Capture held p on falling clock edge, then hold until the next falling edge. Evidence: q starts x, becomes 0 at 55 ns, 1 at 115 ns, and 0 at 175 ns.
semantics.simultaneous_inputs: At 115 ns clock and a fall together; p retains its preceding high-phase value 1 and q captures 1. At 175 ns clock falls while a rises; p and q retain/capture preceding p=0.
semantics.initialization: No initialization or reset: p and q are x at 0..20 ns. First high phase sets p at 25 ns; q remains x until 55 ns.

numeric.widths: All ports and stored values are single bits.
numeric.logic: Four-state simulation checks use case inequality to preserve initial x expectations.

verification.oracle: Replay every original table row at its stated timestamp, with simultaneous clock/a changes and post-settle comparisons to literal original p/q values.
verification.directed: After replay check high-phase transparency, low-phase retention, and falling-edge captures of both zero and one.
verification.completion: Fatal on mismatch or bounded timeout; print PASS only after all checks.

specification_ambiguities: The finite trace cannot distinguish a falling-edge register for q from a low-level transparent latch driven by p, since p is constant while clock is low. Use falling-edge capture, consistent with all observed q transitions.
Behavior for unknown clock or unknown a after initialization is not specified by the supplied binary stimulus.
